```{r}
files <- c("strategy_returns.csv", "performance_summary.csv", "regime_summary.csv",
		   "macro_signals.csv", "run_settings.csv")
paths <- file.path(params$data_dir, files)
if (!all(file.exists(paths))) {
  stop("Missing pipeline outputs. Run targets::tar_make() from the repository root first.")
}
strategy <- readr::read_csv(paths[1], show_col_types = FALSE)
performance <- readr::read_csv(paths[2], show_col_types = FALSE)
regimes <- readr::read_csv(paths[3], show_col_types = FALSE)
signals <- readr::read_csv(paths[4], show_col_types = FALSE)
settings <- readr::read_csv(paths[5], show_col_types = FALSE)
if (!nrow(strategy) || nrow(performance) != 1 || nrow(settings) != 1) {
  stop("Pipeline outputs are empty or inconsistent.")
}
```

## Research status

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (settings$data_vintage == "synthetic_fixture") {
  cat("**SYNTHETIC FIXTURE: software validation only; not economic evidence.**\n\n")
} else {
  cat("**EXPLORATORY: latest-vintage macro data, not a point-in-time investable backtest.**\n\n")
}
cat(sprintf("Sample: %s through %s; %d monthly returns; %d baseline-fallback periods.\n\n",
			performance$start_date, performance$end_date, performance$periods,
			performance$fallback_periods))
if (performance$periods < 60) {
  cat("**Short sample:** fewer than five years of returns. Do not infer reliable regime efficacy from this sample.\n\n")
}
```

Fixed signal lags do not remove publication-timing uncertainty or historical revisions.
The supplied asset returns are a demonstration dataset without documented investable
instrument provenance. The allocation matrices and trading assumptions are illustrative,
not estimated recommendations. A longer sample alone would not establish efficacy.

## Economic definitions and run settings

Both definitions use the change in the inflation rate, not inflation versus deflation:

- **Growth level / inflation direction:** expansion or contraction from the growth rate;
  rising or falling inflation from the change in the inflation rate.
- **Growth direction / inflation direction:** acceleration or deceleration from the
  change in the growth rate; the same inflation-direction measure.

Levels use the configured lookback; directions compare those rates over the configured
direction window. Exact threshold equality uses the expanding/accelerating/rising branch.
Regimes require consecutive confirmations. A pending switch retains the last confirmed
regime; a missing signal resets confirmation and uses the baseline until reconfirmed.
Rates are retained as context, not used in either allocation definition.

```{r}
as_metrics <- function(x) {
  data.frame(metric = names(x), value = vapply(x, function(column) {
	format(column[[1]], digits = 6)
  }, character(1)), row.names = NULL)
}
knitr::kable(as_metrics(settings))
```

## Net performance

Both portfolios rebalance monthly and pay costs on one-way turnover, including drift.
Initial holdings equal the baseline. Costs are deducted before the month's asset returns.
Annualization assumes 12 observations per year. Drawdowns are negative fractions measured
from an initial wealth of one. `active_cum` is the difference between terminal wealths;
`relative_cum` is their ratio minus one. Neither compounds monthly active-return differences.
Information ratio is undefined when tracking error is zero or unavailable; no risk-free
rate or Sharpe ratio is assumed.

```{r}
knitr::kable(as_metrics(performance))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Net wealth, including the initial baseline holdings."
plot_dates <- c(as.Date(format(strategy$date[1], "%Y-%m-01")) - 1, strategy$date)
wealth <- cbind(Baseline = c(1, cumprod(1 + strategy$baseline_return)),
				Tilted = c(1, cumprod(1 + strategy$tilted_return)))
matplot(plot_dates, wealth, type = "l", lty = 1, col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"),
		xlab = "Date", ylab = "Net wealth (initial = 1)")
legend("topleft", legend = colnames(wealth), col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Net drawdowns from each portfolio's running peak."
drawdowns <- apply(wealth, 2, function(x) x / cummax(x) - 1)
matplot(plot_dates, drawdowns, type = "l", lty = 1, col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"),
		xlab = "Date", ylab = "Drawdown (fraction)")
legend("bottomleft", legend = colnames(wealth), col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

## Regime coverage and monthly net returns

These descriptive summaries use the **lagged regime actually applied** to each return.
Sparse or missing regimes are not evidence of robustness. Volatility is undefined for
single-observation groups; confidence intervals are not estimated in this foundation.

```{r}
knitr::kable(regimes, digits = 5)
```

## Signal diagnostics

The following observations show the latest 12 signal months dated no later than the
last return month. Because allocations are lagged, the newest signals may not yet have
been applied. Raw and confirmed labels make confirmation delays visible. The exported
`macro_signals.csv` contains the full history, inputs for both economic definitions,
and labels for the selected definition only.

```{r}
diagnostics <- signals[signals$date <= max(strategy$date),
  c("date", "growth_level", "growth_direction", "inflation_level", "inflation_direction",
	"raw_regime", "regime")]
knitr::kable(tail(diagnostics, 12), digits = 5)
```

## Next research steps

Document investable asset exposures and total-return sources; extend the sample across
cycles; adopt point-in-time vintages and release dates; evaluate costs and thresholds
out of sample. Broader indicator composites and financial-conditions overlays should
be tested incrementally rather than assumed to improve the model.
